state.purpose: Differentiate AI cost optimization by moving from dashboards to proof-before-effect cost-quality optimization using customer historical evidence. Optimize for highest realized owner hourly earnings reached quickly.

world.priorGenerationFinding: U4 cost-of-quality gate had the best balance on owner-time, setup, commoditization and sales friction within the delta generation; U3 had the strongest value ceiling.
marketEvidence: Mercor describes model routing as a cost-quality Pareto optimization problem: use the least expensive model that still meets required performance.
Sword Health reports an internal model-routing/control-plane effort reduced AI costs by 94% and saved more than $1M/year versus standard API usage.
Marlabs reports a customer case where prompt/model routing reduced LLM API costs by more than 50%.
Commercial and open model-routing products already exist, so merely recommending cheaper models is not differentiated.
world.evidenceCaveat: Savings claims are vendor/company-reported and are not proof that this exact external audit will sell.

candidates.name: cost-of-quality-report
candidates.claim: Customer exports existing model/provider cost plus its own accepted/rejected outcome or eval result by workflow. Engine reports cost per accepted outcome and identifies expensive workflows worth investigation. No alternative model replay is run. One paid snapshot can repeat monthly or quarterly.

candidates.name: offline-model-replay-audit
candidates.claim: Customer exports a bounded historical prompt/trace sample plus its existing expected-output, eval label, accepted/rejected outcome, or other quality criterion. The AI factory replays that same corpus against selected alternative models/providers offline, calculates cost and customer-defined quality on the same cases, and returns a reproducible cost-quality Pareto frontier plus projected savings. It makes no production change. One paid audit is delivered from files; the exact same contract can be rerun when models, prices or workloads change.

candidates.name: offline-routing-policy-audit
candidates.claim: Same evidence as V2, but the factory additionally clusters workload types and evaluates offline routing policies that choose cheaper models for subsets while preserving the customer's quality requirement. Output is a reproducible candidate routing policy, projected savings and failure cases. Customer alone decides whether to implement it in production.

candidates.name: recurring-cost-quality-benchmark
candidates.claim: Start with the V2 paid offline replay audit, then sell recurring benchmark refreshes when provider prices, models or customer workloads change. Each run uses the same fixed corpus/schema, compares current production choice with selected alternatives, records cost-quality deltas, and accumulates a versioned decision history. No production routing is owned by the service.

constraints: No production traffic or production credentials are required for the first paid audit.
Customer supplies the historical corpus and quality criterion.
First audit must be bounded enough to execute mostly automatically.
No standard owner review except exception handling.
No proprietary universal benchmark claim; evaluation is customer-corpus-specific.
No semantic PASS/FAIL threshold in Jev evaluation.
